question: A hexagonal prism is cut by an oblique plane. Which method is most appropriate for developing the lateral surface of the truncated prism?
options: Radial line development
Parallel line development
Triangulation development
Approximate development

question: When drawing a true shape of an oblique section through a cylinder, which auxiliary view technique is required?
options: First angle projection auxiliary view perpendicular to the cutting plane
Third angle projection with a partial view
Rabatment of the section plane about its trace
Revolution of the cylinder axis

question: A cone is cut by a plane parallel to one of its generators. The resulting curve of intersection is a:
options: Circle
Ellipse
Parabola
Hyperbola

question: In orthographic projection, the angle between the projection plane and the projectors in first angle projection is:
options: 45 degrees
60 degrees
90 degrees
180 degrees

question: Which of the following correctly describes a right helical spring in a technical drawing context?
options: The helix advances to the right when viewed axially, rotating clockwise
The helix is wound such that it appears to rise from left to right
The helix pitch equals its outside diameter
The helix lead equals half the pitch

question: To find the shortest distance between two skew lines using descriptive geometry, which pair of views is required?
options: Front view and side view only
An elevation showing one line as a point and a related plan view
A plan view showing both lines parallel and a front elevation
A true length view of both lines simultaneously

question: When developing the surface of an oblique cone by triangulation, the first step is to:
options: Divide the base circle into equal parts and find true lengths of all triangular elements
Draw the slant height as a true length line in the front view
Project the apex onto the base plane
Develop the base ellipse using the trammel method

question: A sphere of diameter 60 mm intersects a cylinder of diameter 40 mm whose axis passes through the centre of the sphere. The curve of intersection in the front view appears as:
options: Two straight horizontal lines
Two ellipses
Two circles
Two parabolas

question: In isometric drawing, a circle of 50 mm diameter is represented as an ellipse. The major axis of this isometric ellipse is approximately:
options: 50 mm

question: Which statement about interpenetration of two cylinders of equal diameter with axes at right angles is correct?
options: The curve of intersection is a true ellipse in all views
The curve of intersection appears as two straight lines in the view where both axes are visible
The curve of intersection is a circle in the view perpendicular to both axes
The curve of intersection projects as two straight lines in the view showing one cylinder end-on

question: A point P is 30 mm above the HP and 20 mm in front of the VP. In first angle projection, point P lies in:
options: The first quadrant
The second quadrant
The third quadrant
The fourth quadrant

question: When using the parallelogram method to construct an ellipse given the major and minor axes, the construction is based on:
options: Dividing the circumscribing rectangle into equal proportional strips
Drawing concentric circles of major and minor radii and plotting intersections
Using a trammel set to half the major and minor axes
Rotating the major axis through 90 degrees

question: In the development of a transition piece connecting a square base to a circular top, the method used is:
options: Parallel line development for all surfaces
Radial line development from the circular end
Triangulation, dividing the surface into triangular elements
Approximate development using gore sections

question: A plane is said to be a profile plane when it is:
options: Parallel to both the HP and VP simultaneously
Perpendicular to both the HP and VP
Inclined to the HP and perpendicular to the VP
Inclined to the VP and perpendicular to the HP

question: When determining the true length of a line by the rotation method in descriptive geometry, the line is rotated about:
options: A vertical axis through one of its endpoints until it is parallel to a projection plane
A horizontal axis through the midpoint of the line
An axis perpendicular to both projection planes
The ground line XY until the line becomes a point
